question: Can dense target-state-INDEPENDENT PERCEPTION (original NSD core) identify the subject-specific native ORIENTATION of the reliable shared imagery residual that lies OUTSIDE the small NSD-Imagery visual span, in an imagery-unseen participant, with ZERO target imagery in fitting?
beta: B0 lineage only: NSD-core betas_fithrf (b2-compatible); B1/b3 (GLMdenoise_RR) PROHIBITED

anchor.source: shared NSD-core natural scenes with complete repeat coverage across all 8 subjects
anchor.leakage_guard: exclude ALL NSD-Imagery scene identities (shared1000 overlap) from the anchor pool globally
anchor.common_space: DETERMINISTIC_SRM (same family as O2; tests information support not algorithm)

K_selection: VISION-ONLY nested (LOSO subject x anchor-image blocks); metric CROSS_SUBJECT_NATIVE_PATTERN_RECONSTRUCTION_R; tie smaller K

retention.R_Y_CORE_VISFULL: full core anchor native span (capacity oracle)
retention.CORE_GAIN_OVER_SMALL_VISUAL_SPAN: R_Y_CORE - R_Y_VISFULL_small (recovery threshold median>=0.15 AND >=6/8 positive)

residual_definition: delta_y_perp relative to the FROZEN O2.2 SMALL visual span (never redefined)
residual_orientation_template: shared residual covariance in anchor coords from TRAINING subjects only; rank r in {1..6} nested-CV (LOSO train subject x identity pair); predict target native residual subspace Bhat=W_core_target U_res (ZERO target imagery)
primary_test: PREDICTED_RESIDUAL_RETENTION = ||delta_y_perp P_RESID_PRED||^2/||delta_y_perp||^2 vs random-anchor-subspace null (100 draws) + full-core oracle + small-vision baseline; participant unit N=8; Holm across ventral/lateral
gauge: projectors / singular values / subspace retention only; W_s->W_s Q, U_res->Q^T U_res leaves native predicted projector invariant

phases.C: imagery residual orientation evaluation (only after B passes)

O3_lock: O3_NOT_READY through O2.3A; orientation identifiability is only a representation-feasibility result -- actual shared-operator generalization must be shown in a later O2.3B
interpretation_boundary: dense NSD-core is still substantial TARGET-SUBJECT functional calibration; NOT zero-calibration; NOT 'imagery is visually encoded'; NOT 'shared operator supported'
